No precedent holds. TiKV's hibernate regions, the one on offer, only stop a region's ticks and messages (checked on the web on 2026-11-10: TiDB docs and forum); the peer stays in memory, as CockroachDB's quiesced ranges do. That is the precedent for quiet groups, not for dropping a group from memory. A web search today found no production multi-Raft system that unloads an idle group and loads it on wake. Nearest by rule but in another role: Orleans grains and Durable Objects (an idle unit is unloaded and the next message wakes it); Pulsar loads a topic only when a client opens it. So the state (a dormant mark and a 24-byte record) and the wake rule are fero's.

Novel. Fencing a writer by an epoch is published (Kafka's producer epochs; BookKeeper's ledger fencing; Neon's terms on safekeepers), but in each of those the writer is the log's own proposer, or the epoch lives in a metadata store. Here a Raft group with its own leader also carries a writer entry for a server outside it, and the group's leader checks every append against it (9 rules, E-16). I cannot name a system with that state and those rules.

added.name: Consumer groups (#groups)
added.option: every row that serves P-08 (the groups library)
added.state: In #groups: the members of each consumer group, as rows with leases, and the group's generation. The group's committed cursors are rows written under a fence on the generation.
added.rules: A member joins and renews its lease. The assignment of slots to members is a pure function of the live members and the generation. A cursor commit carries the generation and is refused below it, so a zombie consumer cannot commit.
added.source: DESIGN-V5 5.3 'Consumer groups' and 5.1; REQUIREMENTS P-08; E-30 (the cursor side). On BUY the consumers are JetStream's own, inside outside-log.
added.model: E-30 modelled the cursor and the outputs, not the membership or the generation fence
added.precedent: Kafka's group coordinator (members kept alive by heartbeats under a session timeout, a generation id, an assignment per generation, OffsetCommit refused with ILLEGAL_GENERATION; KIP-848)
added.why: The list has the cursor (sub.cursor) but not the group's member rows and generation, which are named, replicated state with their own rules. Same state, same rules, same role as Kafka's. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

added.name: Queue claims (leases and delivery counts on message rows)
added.option: every row that serves P-09 (the queue library, on the claim op)
added.state: Per message row of a queue: its claim's lease end and its delivery count. A dead-letter resource holds the rows past the limit.
added.rules: take(n) is one claim at the writer: the first n unclaimed rows, leased from writer time, with the count raised. An ack removes the row; a lapsed lease makes it claimable again; past the limit it moves to the dead-letter resource. A take hands over what it has at once (A-10).
added.source: DESIGN-V5 5.3 'Queue'; REQUIREMENTS P-09; AMENDMENTS A-10 (a take hands over what it has at once); E-44 (measured on JetStream: 294 jobs acked once, 6 dead-lettered)
added.precedent: Amazon SQS (a visibility timeout per received message, a receive count, a redrive to a dead-letter queue past maxReceiveCount); Redis Streams' pending entries with delivery counts (XCLAIM)
added.why: Missed by the list, which names the claim op only inside writer-judging. Same state, same rules, same role as SQS. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

added.name: Presence (rows that live while a session lives)
added.option: every row that serves presence (rows: { while: 'session' })
added.state: A session is a row in #sessions with a lease the client renews. Rows written while: 'session' carry its id.
added.rules: Each group's writer follows #sessions and removes a lapsed session's rows, as log entries.
added.source: DESIGN-V5 5.3 'Presence' and 5.1; AMENDMENTS K-11 (session expiry by #sessions' writer time). The registry exists in the rows with D win, pid and txn too, where the list's client-sessions does not put it.
added.precedent: ZooKeeper's ephemeral nodes (a node carries its session's id and is deleted, through the log, when the session expires); etcd's leases with attached keys; across groups, CockroachDB's sqlliveness sessions (system.sqlliveness; holders elsewhere check the session and clean up its claims)
added.why: Missed by the list. Same state (a session with a lease; rows tagged with it), same rule (the rows go when the session lapses), same role. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

added.name: Cluster credentials in #meta (CA envelopes, join tokens, certificates, the rotating secret)
added.option: every row with a metadata group
added.state: In #meta: the cluster CA key as envelopes encrypted to each #meta voter's key; single-use join tokens; one certificate per member and the revoked ones; the cluster secret, current and next.
added.rules: A join spends one join token and gets the member its certificate. A removed member's certificate is revoked. The secret rotates through a window in which both values are valid.
added.precedent: Docker swarm mode (its Raft store holds the cluster CA, the join tokens and the node certificates; `docker swarm join-token --rotate`, `docker swarm ca --rotate`); CockroachDB's join tokens (`cockroach node create-join-token`); kubeadm bootstrap tokens
added.why: Missed by the list: named, replicated state with its own rules. Same state, same rules, same role as swarm mode. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

added.name: Forks (a new resource that starts from the parent's snapshots)
added.option: every row with a metadata group (fero test, TEST-05 and TEST-06)
added.state: In #meta, per fork: a new resource whose groups start from named snapshots and segments of the parent's groups.
added.rules: A fork writes one #meta record per group and copies nothing. The parent may not drop a snapshot or a segment that a fork names.
added.source: DESIGN-V5 6.2 (piece 8: 'a fork is a new resource whose shards start from the parent's shards' snapshots') and 4.1 ('no fork references it'); REQUIREMENTS TEST-05, TEST-06; E-06 (measured)
added.precedent: Neon's branches (a timeline with an ancestor timeline and an ancestor LSN shares the parent's layers, and GC keeps what a branch still needs); Delta Lake's shallow clones
added.why: Missed by the list, which has only the tier's guard 'no fork still reads it'. Same state (a record that names the parent's immutable files), same rules (copy nothing; pin what is named), same role. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

added.name: Recorder of kernel inputs
added.option: every row with a deterministic kernel of its own (OPS-11 d)
added.state: Per process: a recording of every kernel input (whole frames, ticks, disk and object-store completions), with bulk bytes named by journal reference.
added.rules: Every input is recorded before the kernel steps on it. The journal is kept for as long as the recorder's window refers to it. A dump replays byte for byte.
added.source: REQUIREMENTS OPS-11 (d); AMENDMENTS A-09 (three recorder rules, counted there as format rules); E-42 (measured: 1.1 to 1.7 % of a core; BUY and V4 cannot have it)
added.precedent: Aeron Cluster with Aeron Archive (every input to the state machine is recorded in order and can be replayed); VoltDB's command logging (inputs logged, replayed deterministically); rr (record every nondeterministic input, replay exactly)
added.why: A-09 counts it as format rules, but it is durable state (the tape) with a rule that holds the journal's retention, so by DEV-10 (a) it is a mechanism. Recording inputs for an exact replay is published. PD, ISR, SLOG and OBJ are not in E-42's list, so they are left out. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

regrouped.into: two units: (1) the session registry, #sessions (per client life, a lease; one resource in its own group); (2) the per-group session tables (outcomes and floor, tagged by slot)

The registry is also in the rows with D win, pid and txn, for presence (DESIGN-V5 5.3); the added entry presence-rows carries it there. Both units are published, so DEV-01 does not move; DEV-02's pairs can.

regrouped.into: kept as one unit (the restore), but it holds two pieces of state: the epoch high-water mark in the store, which every slot move also writes, and the session generation, which only a restore writes
